lesson.subtitle: Lesson 4 -- Planning Ahead
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Mauricio | Lesson 4 -- Planning Ahead

listenings.text: So, here is my plan for the two weeks. I am not going to try to talk to everybody, because I did that at the last programme and I came home with forty business cards and zero friends. This time I am going to pick five people and actually have a real conversation with each of them. In the sessions, I am going to ask at least one question a day, even a bad one. And I am not going to answer work emails before six in the evening. My team knows. They are going to survive without me. The outcome I want is simple: come back with five people I can call, and one idea I can actually use.

Let me walk you through the shape of the two weeks. Every morning there are two sessions, and a professor will facilitate each one, so it will be discussion and not lecture. Afternoons are group work: you are going to be in a team of six, and the teams will not change. On Wednesday of the second week each team is going to present a case to the whole room, twelve minutes, no exceptions. There will be a panel on the last Thursday with three chief executives, and I promise you the good questions come from the floor, not from the panel. And finally, on Friday, we will finish at midday, because everybody has a flight.

items.situation: Someone asks what you are going to do at the programme. Answer with two plans and one goal.
A colleague says nobody can cover a meeting while you are away. Volunteer a solution on the spot.
Ask two questions about somebody else’s plans for the programme.
Say one thing you are NOT going to do in November, and why.
You want to say the result you hope to get, and the word will not come.
tips: Sorry, how do you say this in English?
I mean what you get at the end ...
the thing you want to happen ...
